notice.title: Why check authorization?
notice.description: This family detects unintended access to protected routes, administration and teams. Run all checks access for your role and rejection of missing or invalid tokens; the foreign-team check skips if no such team exists. Test isolation between two users separately below with a second account; that check creates and removes temporary prompts in both personal spaces. The session-expiry check also runs separately and may take several minutes.

identity.title: Identity and session
identity.subtitle: Checks authenticated access to the three APIs, rejection of missing or invalid tokens, public routes and personal-space identity. Checks that do not apply to this provider are skipped with a reason.
identity.weaver: Check sign-in, onboarding, direct space membership and rejection of invalid credentials.

authorization.title: Authorization
authorization.subtitle: Proves the live API honors the authorization model: platform-admin flags match real endpoint access, protected routes of every backend refuse a missing, malformed or forged token, administration routes follow your platform role, and team content stays closed to a team you do not belong to, even for a platform admin.
authorization.weaver: Verify protected routes and access in the selected space. Run the manual role campaign to check isolation between accounts.

knowledge.title: Documents and knowledge
knowledge.subtitle: Works in your personal space. Checks retrieval scoped to one folder and isolation from another through the self-test agent, direct search under each search policy, one small document per supported format (text, Markdown, JSON Lines, PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint), a SQL query on a CSV, linking and unlinking a document between folders, retrievability, the document tree, that deleted documents leave no retrievable chunk and, as an optional step, the corpus audit.
knowledge.weaver: Upload and retrieve a disposable document in the selected space, then verify cleanup.

agents.title: Agents
agents.subtitle: Enrolls a temporary self-test agent in your personal space. Checks that its system prompt is delivered, that its chat model is usable, that an updated configuration reaches several following turns, that a disabled agent cannot run, the copy targets, a duplicate under a chosen name and the refusal of a second one, a copy under a free name, and concurrent conversations that each receive only their own context.
agents.weaver: Check agent configuration, availability and execution in the selected space.

prompts.title: Prompts
prompts.subtitle: Creates a temporary category and prompt in the selected space. Checks partial edits, commands, favorites, categories, the marketplace listing and cleanup. The server decides whether writes are permitted.
prompts.weaver: Check categories, prompt editing, slash commands, favorites and cleanup. At the organization level, also read the prompt marketplace.

web.title: Web research
web.subtitle: Runs the deterministic web research agent through the real execution pipeline. It fails first when web research is not enabled on this deployment; otherwise it proves each protection holds: refused schemes, ports and credentials, loopback, private, metadata and encoded addresses, platform service names, redirects to internal destinations, binary content, and a SafeSearch the model cannot weaken. Then it checks that search and page reading work. Probes that need an unreachable third-party endpoint are skipped, never passed. The temporary agent is deleted at the end.
web.weaver: Test guarded web access through the diagnostic agent when web research is enabled.

platform.title: Platform
platform.subtitle: Reads the deployment without changing it: service health and readiness, account status, the identity provider and its token issuer, clocks, agent runtimes and the self-test agent, model profiles, the capability catalog and the main admin settings.
platform.weaver: Check service health, sign-in configuration and the selected organization's catalogs.

conversations.title: Conversations
conversations.subtitle: Creates two conversations in your personal space and runs a turn in one. Checks that both are listed, that a rename is kept, that an attached file is retrievable in its conversation and never from the other one, that a deleted attachment disappears, the inactive-conversation list, and bulk deletion.
conversations.weaver: Create disposable conversations and verify that an attachment stays within its conversation.

teams.title: Teams
teams.subtitle: Creates a disposable team you administer, then deletes it. Skipped until you accept the team-admin charter; the run never accepts it for you. Checks that team owner alone cannot edit content, that the editor role opens and its revocation closes editing, a team prompt, folder and agent, wiki revisions and restore, the join link, model routing, copying the team agent to your personal space, and that nothing of the deleted team stays reachable.
teams.weaver: Create and remove a disposable child space using your existing rights.

security.title: Security
security.subtitle: Checks that the platform is served over HTTPS, reports which response-hardening headers the page sets, checks that error responses expose no stack trace, then uploads a harmless SVG to your personal space and checks that its raw download is an attachment and that its inline preview cannot run as a document on this origin.
security.weaver: Check transport, response headers, safe errors, document downloads and previews.

observability.title: Observability
observability.subtitle: Reads the conversation, message and token usage KPIs over the last day, then checks the health of the search cluster and of every metrics target. A backend this deployment does not run is skipped, never failed.
observability.weaver: Read your usage, authorized space usage and Technical status.

search.hybridDescription: Hybrid search combines keyword matching (exact terms, names, IDs) with semantic similarity. It is the best option when your question contains specific terminology (component names, error codes, APIs) but also benefits from conceptual matching. Hybrid typically improves recall while keeping precision high, at the cost of slightly more computation.
search.semanticDescription: Semantic search uses embeddings to retrieve passages that are conceptually similar to your question, even if they don't share the same words. This usually finds the most relevant context for broad or exploratory questions, but it can sometimes include loosely related results when your query is very short or ambiguous.
search.strictDescription: Strict search prioritizes precision over coverage. It applies tighter constraints (e.g., stronger keyword/metadata matching and/or higher similarity thresholds) so only highly confident results are retrieved. Use this when you want to avoid ‘maybe relevant' documents, or when your corpus is large and you prefer fewer, more exact sources. If nothing matches strongly, results may be sparse.
